body_markdown:
**What is your role at Enanta?**
I lead the Commercial and New Product Strategy function, which focuses on incorporating the perspectives of physicians, patients and payers, along with evolving market dynamics, into our drug development decisions. I also serve as a Program Lead, helping guide the strategy and execution of our RSV development program by working closely with colleagues across different functions. Both roles give me the opportunity to shape how we develop assets in our pipeline.


**Why did you join Enanta?**
I joined Enanta in 2022 after working at several other biotech companies. I’ve always enjoyed working at smaller organizations, where there are meaningful opportunities to help shape the development of assets and the direction of the pipeline. That was one of the things that attracted me to Enanta. In fact, one of my first projects involved evaluating opportunities to expand Enanta’s pipeline into therapeutic areas beyond virology, which gave me the opportunity to contribute to the company’s strategic direction early on.


**How did you get into your specific field?**
Biotech is a natural fit for me, combining my background in biochemistry with the problem-solving skills I developed as a management consultant. I began my career in the industry in commercial roles spanning analytics, marketing and market access. Since then, I’ve worked across the entire product lifecycle, from preclinical development through launch, including serving as a Program lead responsible for guiding cross-functional teams through drug development.


**What do you think is the most important challenge for the Biopharmaceutical Industry?**
It’s difficult to balance short-term financial pressures with long-term company strategic priorities, especially with the cyclicality of the biotech industry. In some cases, near-term returns, may not align with the longer timelines required to make the best strategic decisions for a company or its development programs.


**What would be the one word to describe the team at Enanta?**
The Enanta Core Value that first comes to mind is “Respect”.


**What is the best career advice you got when starting out?**
To work hard and be open to feedback.


**What did you like to do when you were young that you wish you could do more as an adult?**
I like my independence too much to wish to go back to being a kid, but I do miss being unplugged from technology. I have some technology breaks every summer when on vacation in the Lakes region of New Hampshire, where it’s great to be fully present with family and friends.


**What do you do for fun when you’re not at work?**
I enjoy cooking and staying active. Lately, I’ve been trying to find a balance between running and weightlifting, since I tend to focus on one at the expense of the other.
